title: Quiz: Food Chains and Food Webs

questions.stem: What do the arrows in a food chain represent?

options.text: The direction of energy flow from food to feeder
The direction an organism moves
Which organism is larger
The direction of water flow

questions.explanation: The arrows in a food chain show the direction of energy flow, pointing from the organism being eaten to the organism eating it. For example, grass -> rabbit means energy flows from grass to rabbit.

options.text: An organism that makes its own food, usually by photosynthesis
An organism that eats other organisms
An organism that breaks down dead matter
An organism that parasitises other organisms

questions.explanation: A producer is an organism that makes its own food, usually through photosynthesis. Green plants and algae are producers. They form the first trophic level and are the source of energy for all other organisms in the food chain.

questions.stem: What is the role of a decomposer in a food chain?

options.text: To hunt and eat other animals
To break down dead organisms and waste, recycling nutrients
To produce food through photosynthesis
To compete with producers for sunlight

questions.explanation: Decomposers (such as bacteria and fungi) break down dead organisms and waste materials, recycling nutrients back into the soil. This makes nutrients available for producers to absorb and use for growth.

questions.stem: How does a food web differ from a food chain?

options.text: A food web is simpler than a food chain
A food web shows multiple interconnected food chains in an ecosystem
A food web only shows producers and consumers
There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: A food web shows multiple interconnected food chains within an ecosystem. It gives a more realistic picture of feeding relationships because most organisms eat more than one type of food and are eaten by more than one predator.

questions.stem: An organism at the second trophic level is called a:

options.text: Secondary consumer
Producer
Primary consumer
Tertiary consumer

questions.explanation: An organism at the second trophic level is a primary consumer (herbivore). The first trophic level is producers, the second is primary consumers, the third is secondary consumers, and the fourth is tertiary consumers.

questions.stem: If a disease kills most of the rabbits in a food web, what would likely happen to the fox population?

options.text: It would increase because foxes would eat the diseased rabbits
It would decrease because foxes would have less food
It would increase because foxes would have less competition
It would not change at all

questions.explanation: If the rabbit population decreases, the fox population would also decrease because there is less food available. This demonstrates interdependence -- changes in one population affect others in the food web.

questions.stem: Which trophic level always has the most energy?

options.text: Secondary consumers
Tertiary consumers
Producers
Primary consumers

questions.explanation: Producers always have the most energy because they capture energy directly from sunlight. Energy is lost at each trophic level (mainly through respiration), so each successive level has less energy available.
